sources.title: Moritz Hardt, Benjamin Recht, and Yoram Singer, Train faster, generalize better: Stability of stochastic gradient descent
sources.locator: Full arXiv preprint; inspected §2.2 Definition 2.1 and Theorem 2.2 with proof, §3.2 gradient-update lemmas, §3.3 convex Theorem 3.8 with proof, and §3.4 nonconvex Theorem 3.12, Lemma 3.11, and complete proof.

contents.name: §2.2, Definition 2.1: randomized uniform replacement stability with expectation over the algorithm's internal randomness
contents.reason: The local definition fixes the same randomized replace-one convention and makes the ordered-sample, test-point, and absolute-outside-expectation requirements explicit.

contents.name: §2.2, Theorem 2.2 and proof: ghost-sample exchange and the expected generalization gap
contents.reason: The local proof reconstructs the full coordinate-replacement argument for a measurable randomized learner and adds explicit integrability conditions.

contents.name: The coordinate-transposition step used inside the proof of Theorem 2.2
contents.reason: The local lemma states and proves the exact finite-product exchangeability interface used by the randomized expected-generalization proof.

contents.name: §3.3, Theorem 3.8 (arXiv numbering): convex SGM stability bound and complete proof
contents.reason: The local argument proves the coupling recurrence and then applies the randomized expected-gap theorem under the same convex, smooth, Lipschitz, and step-size conditions.

contents.name: §3.4, Theorem 3.12, Lemma 3.11, and proof: nonconvex SGM stability for bounded smooth losses and inverse-time steps
contents.reason: The local proof derives a finite per-step kick bound and the exact published rate, including the n-1 denominator and bounded-loss hypothesis.

sources.title: Nikolai Matni, ESE680 Lecture 16: Algorithmic Stability and Stochastic Gradient Descent
sources.locator: Complete 9-page Lecture 16 fetched; inspected §3 Definition 1, Theorem 2 and full proof, and §4 Lemma 2 and Theorem 3 with proof, PDF pp. 3–6.

contents.name: §3, Definition 1: expected uniform stability for randomized algorithms
contents.reason: This independent lecture treatment confirms the randomized internal-randomness convention used by the local definition.

contents.name: §3.1, Theorem 2 and complete proof: stability implies expected generalization by replacing one sample coordinate
contents.reason: The lecture supplies a second complete expected-gap proof for randomized learning rules; the local theorem states the required measurability and integrability explicitly.

contents.name: The coordinate-swap identity in the proof of §3.1 Theorem 2
contents.reason: The local exchangeability lemma isolates the finite IID coordinate-swap used in the lecture's ghost-sample proof.

contents.name: §4, Lemma 2 and Theorem 3 with proof: convex SGD stability from nonexpansive gradient updates
contents.reason: The independent full lecture proof supports the convex update contraction and marginal 1/n changed-example recurrence.

contents.name: §4 note that the nonconvex SGD analysis is detailed in Hardt et al. §3.5
contents.reason: This lecture supplies a pointer rather than a second nonconvex proof; the complete primary nonconvex argument was read in Hardt et al.'s full arXiv version and is proved locally.

sources.locator: Full arXiv preprint; inspected §2.2 Definition 2.1 and Theorem 2.2 with proof, §3.3 Theorem 3.8, and §3.4 Theorem 3.12 with complete proof.

contents.name: §3.3, Theorem 3.8 (arXiv numbering): convex constant-step stability formula
contents.reason: The B-page item substitutes a constant schedule into the A-page theorem and describes only the resulting upper bound.

contents.name: §3.3 Theorem 3.8 and §3.4 Theorem 3.12: convex and nonconvex schedule-dependent formulas
contents.reason: The local example computes the two theorem certificates at fixed parameter values and explicitly makes no general ordering claim.

contents.name: §3.3, Theorem 3.8: the global Lipschitz hypothesis on the convex stability bound
contents.reason: The quadratic witness checks that dropping the global Lipschitz premise can leave uniform replacement sensitivity unbounded; it is explicitly not presented as a counterexample to the theorem.

sources.title: Nikolai Matni, ESE680 Lecture 16: Algorithmic Stability and Stochastic Gradient Descent
sources.locator: Complete 9-page Lecture 16 fetched; inspected §3 randomized stability and expected-gap proof and §4 convex SGD stability proof, PDF pp. 3–6.

contents.name: §4, Theorem 3: convex SGD stability formula for a constant schedule
contents.reason: The lecture independently supports the convex bound used in the schedule substitution.

contents.name: §3.1 and §4: expected-gap and convex stability formulas used in the two-regime calculation
contents.reason: The local example computes the convex-side certificate and uses the primary full paper for the nonconvex-side certificate.

contents.name: §3, Definition 1 and Theorem 2: replacement sensitivity and expected-generalization scope
contents.reason: The example uses the exact replace-one sensitivity definition and clearly limits its witness to failure of the required Lipschitz premise.

contents.name: §4 note referring nonconvex SGD stability details to Hardt et al.
contents.reason: The lecture does not provide the complete nonconvex derivation; that proof is taken from the full primary preprint and reconstructed in the A-page theorem.
